Surah al-Rahman (The Most Merciful)

[Meccan, except verse 29, which is Medinan; its verses number seventy-six or seventy-eight.]

﴿The Most Merciful﴾: Allah, exalted is He.
﴿He taught﴾ whomever He willed.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on Surah 55 (ar-Rahman), verse 3:

﴿He created man﴾, i.e., the human species.
﴿He taught him eloquence﴾: speech.
﴿The sun and the moon [follow] a reckoning﴾ يَجْرِيانِ [they run]
﴿And the star﴾: that which has no stem among the plants. ﴿and the tree﴾: that which has a stem. ﴿prostrate themselves﴾: they submit to what is intended for them.
﴿And the heaven He raised high, and He set up the balance﴾ He established justice.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 8:

﴿That you not transgress﴾ i.e., so that you do not act unjustly ﴿in the balance﴾, meaning that by which something is weighed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 9:

﴿And establish the weight with justice⦆ with justice (bil-'adl) ﴿and do not make the balance deficient⦆ you diminish the thing weighed (al-mawzun)
﴿And the earth — He laid it down for the creatures﴾ He established it ﴿for the creatures﴾, meaning for the creation: mankind, jinn, and others.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 11:

﴿In them is fruit, and palm trees﴾, the well-known, ﴿having sheaths﴾, containers for their ṭalʿ (the spathe that encloses the palm's flower cluster).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 12:

﴿And the grain﴾ such as wheat and barley, ﴿with its husk﴾ the chaff, ﴿and the fragrant plant﴾ the leaves that are scented.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 13:

﴿So which of the favours﴾ (ni'am) ﴿of your Lord﴾, O humankind and jinn, ﴿will you deny?﴾ It is mentioned thirty-one times, and the interrogative here is for affirmation (taqrir), in accordance with what al-Hakim narrated from Jabir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to us Surat al-Rahman until he finished it, then said: 'What is the matter with me that I see you silent? The jinn were better than you in response: whenever I recited to them this verse, ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾, they would say: "Nor do we deny any of Your favours, our Lord; to You is all praise."'"
﴿He created man﴾, Adam, ﴿from clay﴾, dry clay that produces a sound, meaning a ringing noise when struck, ﴿like pottery﴾, which is what has been baked from clay.

Translation:

﴿And He created the jinn﴾ — their father, who is Iblis — ﴿from a smokeless flame of fire﴾ — that is, its pure flame, free of smoke.
﴿Lord of the two easts﴾ the east of winter and the east of summer, ﴿and Lord of the two wests﴾ the west of summer and the west of winter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 19:

﴿He released﴾ (maraja) sent forth ﴿the two seas﴾, the sweet and the salty, ﴿meeting each other﴾ in the sight of the eye.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 20:

﴿Between them is a barrier﴾, a barrier from His power, exalted is He, ﴿they do not transgress﴾: neither of them transgresses upon the other, so that it would mix with it.

﴿يَخْرُجُ﴾ (yakhruju), read with the passive form (bi-l-binā' li-l-maf'ūl) and with the active form (wa-l-fā'il), ﴿مِنْهُمَا﴾ (from them both), meaning from their combined body, which applies to either one of them, namely the salt water. ﴿اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجَانُ﴾ (the pearl and the coral): a red bead, or small pearls.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 24:

﴿And His are the ships﴾ (al-jawari), the vessels ﴿raised high﴾ (al-munsha'at), the newly made, ﴿upon the sea like mountains﴾ (al-a'lam), like mountains in their size and their height.
Qur'anic quotation: ﴿Everything upon it﴾ — that is, the earth, of living creatures — ﴿is passing away﴾, perishing. He used "man" (مَن) by way of giving precedence to the rational beings.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 27:

﴿And there remains the Face of your Lord﴾ [i.e., His Essence], ﴿Lord of Majesty﴾ [i.e., greatness] ﴿and Honour﴾ [bestowed] upon the believers by His blessings upon them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 29:

﴿Everyone in the heavens and the earth asks Him﴾ by speech or by state: what they need of strength for worship, provision, forgiveness and other things. ﴿Every day﴾ (time) ﴿He is in a matter﴾ (an affair) which He brings about in accordance with what He decreed from eternity: giving life and causing death, granting honour and bringing humiliation, enriching and impoverishing, bringing into existence and annihilating, answering the supplicant, giving to the one who asks, and other things.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 31:

﴿We shall surely attend to you﴾ (sanafrugh lakum): we shall intend for your reckoning. ﴿O you two burdens﴾ (ayyuha al-thaqalan): mankind and the jinn.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 33:

﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through; you will not pass except with authority﴾ — that is, with power — ﴿and you have no power to do so.﴾

Note: "تنفذوا" means "to go out" (تخرجوا), and "أقطار" means "regions" (نواحي) of the heavens and the earth. "فانفذوا" is an imperative of incapacitation (أمر تعجيز), meaning a command that expresses the impossibility of the act rather than a real order.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 55, verse 35:

﴿A blazing flame of fire will be sent against you both﴾ It is its pure flame, free of smoke, or flame together with smoke. ﴿And smoke﴾ i.e., smoke with no flame in it. ﴿And you will not be able to defend yourselves﴾ you will not be able to ward that off. Rather, it will drive you to the place of gathering.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 37:

﴿When the sky splits open﴾ it opens up into gates for the descent of the angels. ﴿And it becomes red like a rose﴾ i.e., reddened like it. ﴿Like red leather﴾ like a red hide, contrary to its former state. The answer to "when" (idha) is: how great then is the terror.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 55, verse 39:

﴿So on that Day, no one will be asked about his sin, neither man nor jinn.﴾ About his sin. They will be questioned at another time. ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all.﴾ The jann here, and in what follows, means the jinn, and the ins in both places means the insi (a human being).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 41:

﴿The criminals will be known by their marks,﴾ blackness of faces and blueness of eyes. ﴿so they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet.﴾ ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ The forelock of each of them is joined to his feet, from behind or from the front, and he is thrown into the Fire. And it is said to them: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals used to deny.﴾

﴿Yatufūna﴾ (they go around) yas'awna (they run/hasten); ﴿baynahā wa-bayna ḥamīm﴾ between it and boiling water, meaning hot water; ﴿ān﴾ intensely hot, having reached the utmost heat. They are given it to drink when they cry out for help from the heat of the Fire. It is a defective noun (manqūṣ), like qāḍin.
﴿And for whoever fears﴾, that is, for each of them or for them collectively, ﴿the standing before his Lord﴾, meaning his standing before Him for the reckoning, ﴿so he gave up disobeying Him﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 48:

﴿Dhawatā﴾ is the dual of dhawāt (possessing) in its original form, and its final radical is a yāʾ (dhawā → dhawātā). ﴿Afnān﴾ means branches, the plural of fanan, on the pattern of ṭalal (ṭulal).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 52:

﴿In them is every fruit of two kinds﴾ in this world, or every thing by which one enjoys fruit ﴿two kinds﴾, meaning two types, fresh and dry; and the bitter of them in this world, like the colocynth (ḥanẓal), is sweet [there].

﴿Reclining﴾ is a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) whose governing verb is omitted. The sense is that they will be enjoying themselves. ﴿Upon couches whose linings are of istabraq﴾, meaning what is thick and coarse of dībāj (silk brocade), while their outer surfaces are of sundus (fine silk). ﴿And the fruit of the two gardens is within reach﴾, meaning their fruit is near, attainable by one who stands, sits, or lies down.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (*Tafsir al-Jalalayn*, a classical *tafsir*, or Qur'anic exegesis) on surah 55, verse 56:

﴿Therein﴾ in the two gardens and what they contain of lofty chambers and palaces, ﴿restraining their gaze﴾ restraining their eyes to their husbands, who recline, from among mankind and the jinn, ﴿untouched﴾ not deflowered by them, and they are of the *hur* (maidens of paradise) or of the women of this world, the *munsha'at* (those created anew).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 58:

﴿As if they were the ruby﴾ in clarity, ﴿and the coral﴾, the pearl in whiteness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 60:

﴿Is there any reward for good other than good?﴾ — that is, what is the recompense for obedience (al-ihsan bil-ta'a) except the bestowal of bliss (al-ihsan bil-na'im)?

And besides them (﻿وَمِن دُونِهِمَا) — besides the two gardens mentioned — there are two other gardens (جَنَّتَانِ) also, for the one who fears the standing before his Lord (لِمَن خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 64:

﴿Mudhāmmatān﴾ (dark green), black (sawdāwān) from the intensity of their greenness.
﴿In them are two gushing springs﴾, [two springs] spouting with water.
﴿In both of them are fruit and palm trees and pomegranates﴾. They are among them (i.e., the palm and pomegranate are part of the fruit), and it is said they are other than them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 70:

﴿Therein﴾ i.e., in the two gardens and what is in them, ﴿are good [women]﴾ whose characters are good, ﴿fair﴾ beautiful of face.

﴿Ḥūr﴾ (wide-eyed maidens), intensely black in the pupils of their eyes and intensely white in the whites of their eyes" ﴿﴾ "restrained" ﴿restrained﴾ "within tents" ﴿tents of hollowed pearl, attached to palaces, resembling curtained chambers﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 74:

﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾ "Before them" means before their husbands.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 76:

﴿Reclining﴾ — i.e., their spouses. Its i'rab (grammatical analysis) is as was previously explained. ﴿On green cushions﴾ — the plural of rafrafa, i.e., spreads or pillows. ﴿And beautiful carpets﴾ — the plural of abqariyya, i.e., tanafis (fine rugs or carpets).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 55, verse 78:

﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honour.﴾ It has preceded (in meaning), and the word "ism" (name) is extra (zā'id).
